candidates.official_title: 45 Seville Place, Marion Terrace, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.address: 45 Seville Place, Marion Terrace, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay, two-storey brown-brick house, one of a group of five. M-profile slate roof behind parapet with granite coping; Flemish-bond brickwork over granite plinth; gauged-brick window heads; two-over-two timber sliding sash windows; round-headed entrance in moulded render surround; panelled door, engaged pilasters, granite steps and wrought-iron railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH places the house in the nineteenth-century development of southern Seville Place following the railway's arrival in the 1830s–1840s. Survival of original fenestration and joinery contributes to its architectural significance.

candidates.official_title: 44 Seville Place, Emerald Street, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.address: 44 Seville Place / Emerald Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidates.description_summary: Corner-sited end-of-terrace three-bay, two-storey brown-brick house, one of a group of five. Double-pile slate roof hipped to the north; Flemish-bond brickwork over granite plinth; incised stone street-name plaque on north elevation; varied square- and round-headed openings; original timber sash windows and shutters; moulded entrance, panelled door, granite steps and wrought-iron railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies this as a terminating house in a composed terrace of five. Its corner position and small round-headed windows distinguish the end house; surviving original fenestration and joinery contribute to significance.

candidates.official_title: Emerald Dairy, 43 Seville Place, Emerald Street, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.address: 43 Seville Place / Emerald Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidates.description_summary: Corner-sited terraced two-bay, two-storey former house over basement, with wraparound ground-floor shopfront and four-bay two-storey rear extension. Double-pile hipped slate roof; Flemish-bond brown brick; bracketed cast-iron gutters; red-brick sawtooth eaves; rendered platband retaining raised lettering reading 'Emerald Dairy'. Ground-floor windows are blocked and the shopfront is partly concealed by steel shutters.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH links the terrace to post-railway nineteenth-century development and identifies the retained Emerald Dairy lettering as evidence of the building's former dairy use and local social role. The dairy took its name from adjacent Emerald Street.

candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay, two-storey house over raised basement, one of a group of four. Double-pile pitched slate roof with yellow-brick shouldered chimneystacks, yellow clay pots, bracketed cast-iron gutters and red-brick sawtooth eaves. Rendered walls with moulded quoins and plinth; square-headed window openings with rendered reveals; windows blocked and entrance concealed behind recent steel shutters.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH relates the terrace to development after the railway arrived in the 1830s–1840s and notes that retained bracketed eaves and rendered dressings contribute to the building's significance.

candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay, two-storey house over raised basement, one of a group of four. M-profile slate roof; shared yellow-brick chimneystacks; brown Flemish-bond brickwork over granite plinth; original two-over-two timber sliding sash windows; moulded entrance surround and panelled door with engaged pilasters; granite platform and steps; granite plinth wall and wrought-iron railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes a composed terrace of four houses whose terminating houses have a distinctive single-bay upper storey. The survival of original fenestration, sawtooth eaves and delicate wrought-iron railings contributes to architectural significance.
